text.p: Israeli dollar-linked bonds rose sharply in an otherwise quiet market on Tuesday following the decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): unchanged at 103.04
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 102.1
Volume was low at 135 million shekels.
"Investors are only interested in stocks and the bond market is very quiet," said Miri Dagan at Clal Insurance.

"Since the beginning of the week inflation-linked bonds have not been doing too well. Yields on long bonds (today) rose from 4.1 percent to 4.2-4.3 percent. These bonds made a very big move and now it's time for a correction," Dagan added.
Unlinked bonds closed unchanged, but traders said prices are expected to decline on hopes of falling interest rates.
"Unlinked bonds offer yields of 14 percent. Even for those who predict that the inflation in 1997 will be around nine percent it's still very attractive," said Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities.
"Makams rose on hopes for declining interest rates with yields on the Makam for one year falling to 13.75 percent," Dagan added.

Dollar-linked bonds closed sharply higher following the decline of the shekel. "Despite the rise these bonds did not catch up with the dollar's rise and they should continue to rise on Wednesday," Dagan said.
In the local foreign exchange market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3590 shekels against 3.3510 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
